rationale: Zechariah is identified through Addo and dated under Darius, and his vision promises the rebuilding of God's house in Jerusalem; this supports the prophetic context named in Ezra without claiming that the entire vision is quoted.
The dated arrival notice is expanded by the account of departure from Aoue and arrival in Jerusalem; no identity between the first-month planning date and the later departure day is imposed.

The decree directs the remaining silver and gold to uses pleasing to God; Ezra later identifies the transported silver and gold as holy freewill offerings and entrusts them to priests and Levites for delivery to the temple.
